note: The reference case. Everything here is fixed input, so a correct replay of the recipe is deterministic to the byte on this machine and browser.

case.prompt: a photo of a cat wearing sunglasses, studio lighting
case.seedGenerator: torch.Generator(device='mps').manual_seed(42), diffusers randn_tensor for a [1,4,64,64] float16 latent

latent_raw.note: randn(seed=42) * sigma_0. Convert to NHWC before writing: the recipe's `latent_raw` input is [1,64,64,4].

latent_scaled.regenerate: latent_scaled = latent_raw / 14.648819213552878 (= sqrt(sigma_0^2 + 1)), elementwise in float32 then rounded to float16. Kept as a file so the check does not depend on reproducing torch's RNG.
latent_scaled.note: Convert to NHWC before writing: the recipe's `sample` input is [1,64,64,4].

encoder_hidden_states.role: the reference embedding, for checking the text graph in isolation. The end-to-end run does NOT use it: the image graph is fed the text graph's own output.

textGraph.toleranceBasis: 2x the float16-on-MPS noise floor of 2.3e-2, which is the workbench's accuracy gate

imageGraph.sha256Note: sha256 of the 1,048,576-byte readback of the `out` MLTensor, little-endian int32, RGBA-packed. Recorded on the reference machine by scripts/verify.mjs; stable across runs within a session and across separate graph builds.
imageGraph.alpha: every pixel's high byte must be 0xFF

expected_image.png.what: The workbench pass-four run of this graph (bench/results/webnn-e2e-pass4-best.png), for reference. NOT bit-comparable: see notExactWhy.
expected_image.png.notExactWhy: That run bound ONE graph output (`out`); this recipe was recorded with the debug `latent` output on and so declares two. A different output list is a different Core ML graph, compiled and scheduled differently, and float16 reductions reassociate. The result is a max byte difference of 2 on an 8-bit image, i.e. rounding, not a different picture.

reference_image.png.what: Native PyTorch MPS, diffusers, float16 + TAESD, same prompt and seed. A different runtime, so not bit-comparable.

observed.note: 44.28 dB is the headline quality number for this recipe. The float16-on-MPS chain itself reaches only 45.36 dB against the fp32 CPU chain, so the recipe is within about 1 dB of the precision floor.

tolerance.primary: sha256 of the RGBA int32 readback equals expected.imageGraph.sha256. Every input is fixed and the graph has no RNG, so a correct replay is deterministic on the recorded machine and browser.
tolerance.secondary: PSNR >= 55 dB and max RGBA byte difference <= 2 against expected_image.png; PSNR >= 40 dB against reference_image.png; alpha 255 everywhere.
tolerance.fallback: On a different Chrome, macOS or Core ML build, exactness is not guaranteed. Then the secondary bars alone decide, and the sha256 should be re-recorded with a note naming the build.
tolerance.whatBreaksExactness: A different browser or OS build may pick a different kernel or reassociate a reduction. Changing the recipe`s declared output list is enough on its own: see expected.images[expected_image.png].notExactWhy.

quality.bar: image PSNR >= 40 dB against the fp32 chain
